properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The repository's core crypto: secp256k1 private keys are generated, clamped to the curve order (PublicKeyBytes.java:48, PrivateKeyValidator), turned into public keys via EC scalar multiplication on CPU (PublicKeyBytes) and GPU (the vendored hashcat inc_ecc_secp256k1.{h,cl} plus inc_ecc_secp256k1custom.cl compiled at runtime via OpenCLContext), then hashed to Bitcoin addresses. The curve is fixed by the Bitcoin protocol — changeable only by Bitcoin itself, not by this repo; recorded as the protoc

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped vendored hashcat header; no kernel in this application calls Keccak — the address pipeline hashes with SHA-256 + RIPEMD-160. SHA-3 is itself PQ-resistant; recorded as shipped-library API surface, not application use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped vendored hashcat header; no BLAKE2 call site in this application. BLAKE2 is PQ-resistant; recorded as shipped-library API surface, not application use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The randomness source feeding Bitcoin private-key generation, configurable at runtime. Strong default branch is SecureRandom.getInstanceStrong(); the SHA1PRNG branch is a SHA-1-based legacy DRNG that becomes fully deterministic when customSeed is configured, and is deliberately left unseeded in the 'simulate bug' path (CWE-339 posture). The weak java.util.Random branches of the same switch are inventoried separately under ALG-7d1fdc12.
